articles.title: Zelenskyy criticises Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russia as 'wrong' - CNA
articles.summary: Zelenskyy criticises Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russia as 'wrong'  CNAZelensky criticises Trump’s waiver of sanctions on Russia as ‘wrong’  The Straits Times'‘It’s easier dealing with Trump than Putin,’ Zelenskyy tells Euronews amid US tensions  Yahoo News SingaporeHow Zelensky Decided to Take the Risk and Publicly Confront Trump  WSJZelensky: Pressuring Ukraine is simply unfair  Breakingthenews.net
articles.full_text:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia days before they were to take effect will "unfortunately" lead to additional relief for Russia and lead to further Russian aggression, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy posted on Saturday (Oct 17).
"The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me," Zelenskyy wrote on X. "It definitely helps only the Russians."
An executive order issued by Trump on Friday night waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas, that had been scheduled to start next week under the legislation known as the Graham Act that he signed into law last month.
Trump said the waiver was in the national interests of the United States.
The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022. Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticising Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader.
Zelenskyy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin and encourages more attacks by Russia.
"It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people," wrote Zelenskyy, who said Russia on Friday struck more than 15 Ukrainian power generation and transmission sites. "This certainly does not stop the war."
The Ukrainian leader accused Russia of planning to ramp up strikes in western Ukraine. "Is Russia preparing for this? I think so," Zelenskyy wrote.
Russia's investment envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, on Friday called the Trump waiver "a truly historic moment," posting on X that had the penalties taken effect, they could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt.
Weeks before US midterm elections in which Trump's Republicans are battling to maintain their narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further raising oil prices as Americans face increased costs largely attributed to the US-Israeli war on Iran, analysts have said.
Trump signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September.
The legislation, whose primary backer in Congress was the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican, would have imposed tariffs of up to 100 percent within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions.
Countries such as China and India, which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, however, had raised concerns about the Graham Act.
Beijing has said it "consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law" while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties.
But the Graham Act also allows the president to waive sanctions by informing Congress that he has determined that they are not in the national interest. Friday's executive order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action is appropriate."
US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, said Trump was giving in to Putin.
"Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer said in a statement on Friday.
Graham, who died in July, strongly supported US assistance to Ukraine. The passage of the bill named for him had provided hope that there would be continued bipartisan support for Kyiv, wrote Zelenskyy, who lamented the late senator's absence.
"It’s difficult without him, I’ll be honest," Zelenskyy posted on Saturday.
The Ukrainian leader predicted that the US under Trump will continue sanctions relief for Russia beyond Friday's waiver and the diesel export agreement announced earlier this month.
"I think the diesel deal and the move regarding the Lindsey Graham Act are not the end of it. Unfortunately," Zelenskyy wrote.

articles.full_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) will continue to expand and strengthen Malaysia's export markets through initiatives under the 2027 Budget.
Deputy Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Miti, through the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, would lead export-strengthening initiatives through the RM60 million Export Capacity Building Programme and the RM50 million Export Strengthening and Market Diversification Fund.
The initiatives would also be supported by RM1 billion in financing facilities from Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd and RM10 million through EXIM Bank.
"Through 200 export promotion activities, the programme is expected to directly benefit more than 3,500 local companies, with export sales targeted to reach RM12 billion by the end of 2027," he said in a statement.
The deputy minister said efforts to facilitate business would also be intensified through collaboration between the Malaysia Productivity Corporation and the Special Task Force on Agency Reform to reduce bureaucratic red tape.
He revealed that the regulatory reform initiative had so far helped save industries RM3.71 billion in compliance costs and expedite business licence approvals.
Sim said Miti is also focusing on developing viable regional industrial clusters to promote balanced economic growth nationwide. The comprehensive and integrated implementation of these initiatives was expected to enhance Malaysia's standing as a leading regional investment destination and a sustainable global trade hub.
"These efforts include the ministry's strategic initiatives to drive the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, develop automotive and maritime hubs in Perak, and strengthen the semiconductor chip technology ecosystem in Penang and Kedah," he added.
"They also involve expanding trade corridor infrastructure in Perlis and developing a planning framework for a Special Economic Zone in Sibu, Sarawak."

articles.title: The Ministry of Industry and Trade is striving to accelerate the achievement of growth targets for the fourth quarter of 2026. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: The Ministry of Industry and Trade is striving to accelerate the achievement of growth targets for the fourth quarter of 2026.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
|  | 
| Based on the performance results and the growth requirements for the whole year, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has determined a single operational scenario, aiming to achieve the targets for 2026, with a specific roadmap for each of October, November, and December. (Source: Industry and Trade Newspaper) | 
 Accordingly, out of the 8 growth targets assigned by the Government , 6 targets have been achieved or exceeded the implementation schedule after 9 months of 2026. The industrial production index (IIP) increased by approximately 12.3%; total electricity production and imports reached 266.58 billion kWh, an increase of 9.65%; and the power generation capacity reserve ratio reached approximately 25.97%.
 In the first nine months of 2026, exports increased by 24.5%; total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue increased by 13.4%; and the percentage of businesses applying e-commerce reached 61%. In September alone, export turnover reached US$59.48 billion, an increase of 39.1% compared to the same period last year; the trade balance recorded a surplus of US$1.27 billion.
 Two key targets to focus on in the fourth quarter are total power generation capacity and the growth rate of B2C e-commerce. These are areas identified by the Ministry of Industry and Trade as requiring close monitoring and management to ensure the achievement of the 2026 targets. Currently, total power generation capacity stands at approximately 85,594.88 MW, requiring an additional 2,570.12 MW to reach the minimum scale of 88,165 MW by the end of the year. Meanwhile, the B2C e-commerce market grew by 19.5%, 0.5 percentage points lower than the lowest target of 20-22%.
 Based on the performance results and the growth requirements for the whole year, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has identified a single operational scenario, aiming to achieve the 2026 targets, with a specific roadmap for October, November, and December. The results exceeding the schedule in the first nine months are considered a safe margin and will not be used to adjust the operational requirements downwards in the remaining months of the year.
 For exports, the focus of management has shifted to maintaining a reasonable growth rate, improving the quality of growth, controlling the origin of goods, limiting trade risks, and reducing dependence on the foreign direct investment (FDI) sector.
 A notable aspect of the new scenario is the application of a three-tiered risk management mechanism (green, yellow, and red) for each indicator on a monthly basis. When an indicator reaches the warning threshold, the lead unit must immediately activate the prepared solutions, without waiting for the quarterly assessment results. Importantly, an indicator must not remain at the Red level for more than one month without a solution being implemented and reported.
 This approach shows that the operational requirements of the Ministry of Industry and Trade are shifting strongly from evaluating results to proactively identifying, preventing, and handling risks, closely monitoring actual developments to promptly adjust solutions.
 According to the updated scenario, the average Industrial Production Index (IIP) for the remaining months of the year is expected to reach approximately 12.5-13%, ensuring that the annual growth rate remains within the target range of 12-14%. Total electricity production and imports in the fourth quarter are estimated at approximately 88.55 billion kWh, bringing the total annual output to approximately 355.13 billion kWh, an increase of about 9.92%. Annual export turnover is expected to increase by approximately 22.8%, while total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue are projected to increase by approximately 13.3%.
 For B2C e-commerce, the projected growth rates for October, November, and December are 21%, 23%, and 26%, respectively, bringing the annual growth rate to approximately 20.5%. The percentage of businesses adopting e-commerce is expected to reach around 68%, approximately 6 percentage points higher than the upper limit of the target.
 To realize these goals, the Ministry of Industry and Trade requests that efforts be made to maximize the year-end shopping peaks and the 2026 Online Friday shopping event; coordinate with major e-commerce platforms to implement programs promoting the consumption of Vietnamese goods, supporting shipping and payment costs. At the same time, it calls for promoting the listing of businesses, cooperatives, and OCOP products on these platforms, and expanding logistics and digital payment services in rural areas.
 The Department of E-commerce has been tasked with shifting its focus from expanding the number of participants to increasing actual transactions. Key tasks include strengthening seller verification, ensuring transparency of product information, managing livestreaming activities, affiliate marketing, and cross-border e-commerce; and improving methods for measuring the size of the B2C e-commerce market, ensuring that the data accurately reflects reality.
 For the electricity sector, the Ministry of Industry and Trade requires the creation of a list of contingency projects with a total capacity of no less than 120% of the remaining capacity shortfall, equivalent to approximately 3,100 MW. Along with this, it calls for accelerating the process of granting commercial operation certificates (COD) for each unit and each part of the project that meets the criteria; shortening the testing and acceptance time to bring power sources into operation as soon as possible.
 In the domestic market sector, key tasks include implementing the second national concentrated promotional program, carrying out the "Vietnamese people prioritize using Vietnamese goods" campaign, proactively preparing goods for Tet (Lunar New Year), and implementing solutions to stabilize the market.
 Regarding export activities, the Ministry of Industry and Trade focuses on controlling the origin of goods, improving the effectiveness of free trade agreements (FTAs), and expanding markets in the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, and Halal markets.
 Updating growth scenarios on a monthly basis, linked to risk warning mechanisms and specific responsibilities of each unit, provides a foundation for the Ministry of Industry and Trade to proactively address bottlenecks, focus resources on challenging targets, and resolutely achieve the 2026 growth target and create a foundation for development in 2027.

articles.title: The Prime Minister's report to the National Assembly highlights the contributions of the Ministry of Industry and Trade in 2026. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: The Prime Minister's report to the National Assembly highlights the contributions of the Ministry of Industry and Trade in 2026.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
The Prime Minister's report to the National Assembly on the morning of October 17 highlighted the contributions of the Ministry of Industry and Trade: Industry and construction achieved the highest growth since 2015; and imports and exports exceeded 1 trillion USD for the first time.
On the morning of October 17th, at the opening session of the 2nd meeting of the 16th National Assembly, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung presented the Report on the results of implementing the socio-economic development plan for 2026 and the projected plan for 2027. According to the Report, the economy in 2026 is expected to achieve and surpass 14 out of 15 key targets. GDP in the third quarter increased by 9.95%, and in the first nine months by 9.01%, placing it among the highest in the region and the world.
The report highlights many outstanding achievements in areas under the management of the Ministry of Industry and Trade, such as industrial production, electricity supply, petroleum products, import and export, and attracting investment in processing and manufacturing.
Industry is growing at its fastest rate in over a decade.
According to the report, the industrial and construction sector grew by 11.21% in the first nine months, the highest rate since 2015. This was the fastest-growing sector among the three economic sectors, while agriculture remained stable and the service sector developed positively.
Foreign capital flows strongly into industry. Registered FDI capital in the first nine months reached US$50.36 billion, an increase of 76.4%, the highest since 2021. The Prime Minister emphasized that this capital flow "concentrated heavily in processing, manufacturing, high technology, electronics, and semiconductors." Total social investment in the first nine months reached VND 3.11 trillion, an increase of 15.1%.
The quality of Vietnam's exported industrial goods is recognized globally . According to the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), the Global Innovation Index 2026 ranked Vietnam 43rd out of 139 countries, an increase of one position. Vietnam leads the world in the proportion of high-tech exports and the proportion of innovative goods exports in total merchandise trade.
Imports and exports surpassed the $1 trillion mark for the first time.
Total import and export turnover in the first nine months increased by 30.4%. The report estimates that the whole year will reach $1.11 trillion, exceeding the $1 trillion mark for the first time. This marks a new milestone in the scale of trade for the economy.

These results are partly due to integration efforts. The report indicates that in the first nine months, Vietnam upgraded relations with seven partners; the government actively negotiated trade agreements with partners; and high-level diplomatic efforts contributed to mobilizing resources and expanding markets. Simultaneously, efforts to combat smuggling, origin violations, and intellectual property infringement were strengthened.
Maintain sufficient electricity and fuel supplies amidst sharply rising global prices.
Energy is an area that the Prime Minister has devoted considerable time to within the overall picture of macroeconomic stability. The report shows that, despite the sharp increase in crude oil prices and many strategic commodities, and conflicts causing disruptions to global supply chains, under the guidance of the Party, the Government, and the Ministry of Industry and Trade, many targets have achieved very commendable results.
Regarding petroleum products, the government has boosted domestic production, diversified import sources, and promptly utilized tax and fee instruments, as well as state budget allocations. As a result, supply has been ensured, and petroleum prices have been kept low compared to the region.
Regarding electricity, the rational mobilization and regulation of power sources helps ensure supply and prevent price increases, even though electricity demand is at its highest level ever. The report clearly indicates that this demand stems from growth targets, investment in science and technology, and data centers.
These two results, along with effective price management and control, helped keep the average consumer price index for the first nine months at only 4.52%. Energy is a key input for all industries; therefore, maintaining the supply and price levels of electricity and fuel means keeping costs down for businesses and purchasing power for the people.
In terms of institutional aspects, the Report indicates that the Government has submitted numerous laws and resolutions to the National Assembly to thoroughly address long-standing outstanding issues, "especially projects related to land, energy, and healthcare." The Government has also perfected the political and legal framework to definitively resolve obstacles to wind power, solar power, and mineral projects.
By the end of September, the whole country had 4,688 outstanding projects that had been processed or had solutions in place, covering a total area of nearly 196,000 hectares and with a total investment of over 3.2 trillion VND. The report does not separate the energy projects from this figure.

With the year drawing to a close, the government has set a target of achieving double-digit growth. Of the seven task groups, the first group includes many responsibilities of the Ministry of Industry and Trade: ensuring the supply of electricity and petroleum products; boosting the domestic market through measures to stimulate demand and capitalize on the year-end consumption season while controlling and stabilizing prices; and promoting exports and reducing the trade deficit.
Actions of the Ministry of Industry and Trade
These requirements will be concretized at this session through three draft laws submitted to the National Assembly by the Minister of Industry and Trade, acting on behalf of the Prime Minister, according to the Session Program:
The three pillars of the nine-month results were accelerated industrial growth, trade exceeding targets, and stable energy. This provides a foundation for the sector to enter the final quarter of the year with the task of maintaining electricity and fuel supply, stimulating consumer demand, and reducing the trade deficit as required by the Government.

articles.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump - CNA
articles.summary: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump  CNATrump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies  BBCTrump’s Russia sanctions waiver called mistake by Republican Party allies  The Straits TimesTrump Offers Putin Economic Relief in Hopes That Russia Will Return the Favor  The New York TimesTrump paused Russia sanctions to ‘analyse’ impact on global economy: Rubio  The Straits Times
articles.full_text:
US President Donald Trump's reversal on the Russia sanctions comes after he struck a deal with Russia President Vlamidir Putin to ease sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel into global markets.
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday (Oct 16) that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia's energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington's ties with war-torn Ukraine.
The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv's fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump's support slumped.
The Lindsey Graham Act – named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill – had allowed Trump the authority to impose duties up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas.
The legislation, which Trump signed into law last month, targeted Russia's energy and defence sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials, as well as Moscow's so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent Western sanctions.
Trump's reversal on the Russia sanctions comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel into global markets.
A Russian presidential envoy on Saturday called Trump's decision a "historic moment".
"The Trump administration's suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment," Kirill Dmitriev said on social media.
The Kremlin and Putin, who appeared in military uniform on Friday and said Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine, have not yet reacted to the move, which is a major diplomatic win for Russia.
The US president's war in Iran has sparked crippling oil shortages and price spikes, creating major headwinds for his Republican Party ahead of midterm elections next month.
Asked if he was being made a scapegoat for Trump's domestic woes ahead of the vote, Zelensky just smiled.
"This is my answer," he told journalists in Brussels, after an extended pause.
In another sign of strained relations between the United States and Ukraine, Trump branded Kyiv's actions a "disgrace" after Zelensky ordered his forces to resume strikes on Russian refineries.
"I defend the interests of Ukraine and the Ukrainian people exclusively," Zelensky said after talks with EU leaders.
The breakdown between Trump and Zelensky has fuelled fears that the US leader is siding with Moscow.
Those concerns have been heightened by disruptions to a critical US-provided satellite system that has hampered Ukraine's ability to counter Russia's intense bombardments.
Ukraine uses technology from Elon Musk's SpaceX for battlefield communications, but the tech billionaire – a virulent Zelensky critic – said his company was not behind the disruption, while a US official denied any intervention by Trump.
"INCREASE PRESSURE"
European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky as he grappled with Trump.
"This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia's sanctions," European Council chief Antonio Costa said.
"Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure."
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that "the situation in Ukraine is currently truly dire, with numerous Russian attacks and a tense relationship between Ukraine and the US."
"It is crucial that we, as Europe, demonstrate our unconditional support for them today – and explore what additional steps we can take," he said.
Zelensky asked the bloc – Ukraine's biggest international backer – to provide more Patriot missiles to shoot down Russian missiles and come up with an extra 70 billion euros (US$79 billion) in support next year to help Kyiv keep fighting.
Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defences ahead of winter, when temperatures can plummet to as low as -20 degrees Celsius and Moscow's attacks threaten electricity, heating and water systems.
Russian strikes on the southern cities of Kherson and Zaporizhia killed a 64-year-old man and at least 17 people, including an 11-year-old girl, Ukrainian authorities said Saturday.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen confirmed that Zelensky's 70-billion euro plea "has to be covered" and urged partner countries to "step in" and help.
French President Emmanuel Macron said Kyiv's backers will analyse the demand, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the European Union will discuss it before the end of the year.
The EU is currently paying out instalments of a 90-billion-euro loan for Kyiv that was set to help cover funding to the end of 2027.
But Ukrainian authorities have warned they will still face a major budget black hole as Russian strikes have battered the country's economy.
The talks on new funding have reignited calls for the EU to tap around 200 billion euros in frozen Russian central bank assets to fund Ukraine.
"The frozen assets are there. That's what should be used for supporting Ukraine," said Latvian premier Andris Kulbergs.
But there seems little momentum on that front as Belgium, where most of the funds are held, remains opposed.

Miss Universe CEO addresses eligibility of 6 Southeast Asian representatives
Responding to a statement by Nawat Itsaragrisil, CEO of Miss Universe Eastern Pte. Ltd., Day said decisions concerning the Miss Universe pageant fall under the authority of the Miss Universe Organization, which he leads.
He cited decisions concerning contestants, contracts for host venues and show production as matters under the organization's authority.

The controversy has emerged amid disagreements over the rights to organize, distribute and manage the pageant in certain markets.

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's third-quarter 2026 advance gross domestic product (GDP) estimate of 5.3 per cent is a positive surprise despite external shocks, particularly the ongoing US-Iran conflict, economists said.
They told Business Times that while growth moderated from six per cent in the preceding quarter, the slowdown did not necessarily signal a broad-based loss of economic momentum.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said proactive government measures, including targeted fuel subsidies through MyKad introduced last year, had helped cushion the economy against external shocks.
Petroliam Nasional Bhd's efforts to secure fuel supplies from outside the Strait of Hormuz also helped minimise disruptions to domestic economic activity, he added.
Foreign investor interest in Malaysia and stronger demand for technology-related sectors had also supported growth, while full employment and relatively contained inflation helped sustain consumer spending.
"Overall, it is a positive surprise and it looks like the growth numbers could be surprised on the upside with the prevailing GDP growth projection currently standing between 4.8 per cent to 5.3 per cent," the economist said.
He added that growth of 5.3 per cent would put Malaysia's economy above its estimated trend growth rate of around 4.7 per cent.
According to the advance estimate released by the Statistics Department today, Malaysia's GDP is estimated to have grown 5.3 per cent in Q3, slightly higher than the 5.2 per cent recorded in the corresponding period last year.
Bank Negara Malaysia is scheduled to release the official Q3 GDP figures on Nov 18.
Growth eased from six per cent in the preceding quarter, with all economic sectors expanding except mining and quarrying.
For the first nine months of 2026, the economy grew 5.5 per cent, compared with 4.8 per cent in the same period last year.
The services sector remained the main growth driver, expanding 5.4 per cent, supported by wholesale and retail trade, information and communication, as well as finance and insurance activities.
Manufacturing growth accelerated to 7.5 per cent from 7.3 per cent in the preceding quarter, driven by export-oriented industries, particularly electrical, electronic and optical products, as well as petroleum, chemicals, rubber and plastics products.
Construction growth eased to six per cent from 6.5 per cent, supported by non-residential projects, particularly data centres, and specialised construction works.
The agriculture sector rebounded 1.3 per cent after contracting 3.7 per cent in the preceding quarter, driven by oil palm and livestock activities.
In contrast, mining and quarrying contracted 4.9 per cent, reversing the 9.2 per cent expansion recorded in the second quarter, following a decline in crude oil and condensate production.
Despite the expansion, Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said Malaysia should remain mindful of risks stemming from its exposure to global trade and the current AI investment cycle.
He said softer global technology spending could weigh on semiconductor exports, manufacturing activity and data centre investments.
Higher oil prices could raise businesses' operating costs and further erode household purchasing power.
"Another concern is whether domestic consumption can remain strong if wages fail to keep pace with living costs.
"Malaysia should therefore strengthen domestic economic resilience by improving productivity, supporting small and medium enterprises, attracting higher-value investments and developing new export markets.
"The priority is not simply to maintain headline growth, but to ensure that growth is broad-based and sustainable, so the economy can withstand external shocks without placing excessive pressure on households or public finances," Idham said.
He said Malaysia remains on a relatively solid growth trajectory, but sustaining this momentum will depend on domestic demand, the quality of investments and efforts to diversify the economy's growth drivers.

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is on track to exceed the official full-year gross domestic product (GDP) growth expectation of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent after the economy expanded by 5.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, said economists.
The Finance Ministry, in its Economic Outlook 2027 report, has raised its 2026 real GDP growth projections to 4.8 to 5.3 per cent, up from 4.0 to 4.5 per cent in Budget 2026.
Prof Dr Yeah Kim Leng, director of the economic studies programme at the Jeffrey Cheah Institute of Sunway University, said the third-quarter (3Q) GDP expansion of 5.3 per cent affirms the economy's resilience despite continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.
"With growth hitting 5.5 per cent in the first three quarters, the economy is on track to exceed the full-year official 4.8–5.3 per cent GDP growth expectation," he told Bernama.
Yeah said growth moderated slightly compared with the previous quarter but held up well against the challenging external backdrop of continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.

"Encouragingly, the manufacturing sector picked up pace, indicating sustained export demand not only for high-value electronics and optical products but also resource-based chemicals, plastics and rubber products that have higher domestic value added," he added.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest GDP performance was a positive surprise, with growth potentially surprising on the upside against the prevailing projection of between 4.8 per cent and 5.3 per cent.
"At 5.3 per cent, the Malaysian economy is seen to be growing above its trend level of around 4.7 per cent," he said.
Mohd Afzanizam said positive appetite among foreign investors to invest in Malaysia, along with greater demand for the technology-related sector, helped sustain economic growth momentum.
Full employment also helped maintain steady consumer spending as inflation remained fairly contained, he added.
Earlier today, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) announced in its advanced estimates report that Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in 3Q 2026, after registering 6.0 per cent growth in the preceding quarter, while for the first three quarters of 2026, the economy achieved growth of 5.5 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in 2025's corresponding period.
Domestic demand and E&E to sustain growth
Meanwhile, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) is maintaining its 2026 GDP growth projection at 5.4 per cent, with its autoregression and leading economic index models pointing to sustained growth momentum of 5.0–5.2 per cent in the second half of the year (2H 2026).
"Robust growth of 5.7 per cent in 1H 2026, together with today's 5.3 per cent growth reading, which was in line with our in-house expectation, reinforces our constructive outlook.
"Looking ahead, economic activity is expected to remain supported by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electrical and electronics (E&E) exports," it said in a research note today.
RHB IB said private consumption is projected to remain firm, underpinned by healthy labour market conditions, continued income growth and civil servant salary adjustments.
"Private investment should also remain resilient, driven by infrastructure projects, ongoing data centre developments and capacity expansion in manufacturing.
"Meanwhile, continued digitalisation, automation and favourable global demand should encourage further investment, particularly in manufacturing and information and communication technology," it said.
In a separate note, Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd has also maintained its full-year growth forecast at 5.3 per cent, although the stronger-than-expected advance estimate points to an upside risk to its forecast.
It said any revision would hinge on September's data and the full GDP release.
"Domestic demand should increasingly drive growth in the 2H 2026, backed by resilient consumer spending, strong services activity and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital infrastructure.
"Implementation of approved projects, rising household incomes, and a firm labour market add further support," it said.
Kenanga said that manufacturing should remain a key driver on sustained E&E demand from AI and data centre expansion, although growth may slow as front-loading fades.
External risks remain, OPR hold expected
Mohd Afzanizam said the Malaysian economy remained fairly resilient despite external shocks, especially the ongoing war in Iran, which is likely to affect global supply chains and fuel costs.
He said proactive government measures, such as targeted fuel subsidies via MyKad since last year, along with efficiencies demonstrated by Petroliam Nasional Bhd in procuring fuel supplies beyond the Strait of Hormuz, had allowed the economy to operate almost seamlessly.
RHB IB, however, said geopolitical tensions in West Asia, commodity price volatility and shifting trade policies pose risks to the outlook.
"Prolonged tensions and elevated oil prices could raise production and transportation costs while dampening global demand," it said.
Separately, CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said the stronger third-quarter outturn points to a modest overshoot of its 5.0 per cent growth forecast for 2026, which would be revised after the full 3Q GDP release in November.
"Stronger external demand remains supportive of the manufacturing outlook, particularly in E&E, where manufacturers have reported longer order books," it said.
Despite the GDP upside, CIMB retained its expectation for Bank Negara Malaysia to hold the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent in November, given signs of moderating domestic activity and contained inflation.
RHB IB also expects the OPR to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the November Monetary Policy Committee meeting, saying the current economic environment and inflation trajectory support a broadly stable policy outlook.
DOSM said the preliminary GDP, which provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of economic performance for 3Q 2026, will be released on Nov 18, 2026.
-- BERNAMA

articles.title: The Ministry of Industry and Trade is closely following the growth scenario and is determined to achieve the targets for 2026. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: The Ministry of Industry and Trade is closely following the growth scenario and is determined to achieve the targets for 2026.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
After nine months, many indicators in the Industry and Trade sector have met or exceeded targets. The Ministry of Industry and Trade is managing the plan on a monthly basis, aiming for comprehensive achievement of the 2026 goals.
According to data from the Institute for Strategic Studies and Public Policy ( Ministry of Industry and Trade ), after nine months of 2026, six out of eight growth targets assigned by the Government to the industry have been met or exceeded. This result is recorded in the context of the national economy maintaining high growth momentum, with GDP in the first nine months estimated to increase by 9.01% compared to the same period last year, the highest level in the past 15 years.
Industrial production continues to affirm its role as the main driver of growth. The Industrial Production Index (IIP) for the first nine months increased by 12.3% compared to the same period last year, the highest increase for the same period since 2019, recording growth in all 34 localities. The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) for the manufacturing sector in September reached 51.9 points, continuing to remain above the 50-point threshold, indicating that business conditions in the manufacturing sector continue to improve, although the rate of improvement is slower than the previous month.
Export activities continued to record positive results. Merchandise export turnover in the first nine months reached US$434.30 billion, an increase of 24.5% compared to the same period last year, exceeding the target growth rate of 15-16% set for the whole year. In September alone, the merchandise trade balance recorded a surplus of US$1.27 billion, although the overall trade deficit for the first nine months remained at US$19.42 billion.
The domestic market maintained stable growth. Total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue in the first nine months increased by 13.4% compared to the same period last year. The percentage of businesses applying e-commerce reached 61%. In the energy sector, the power capacity reserve ratio reached approximately 25.97%, 4.17 percentage points higher than the 21.8% figure.
Based on the results of the first nine months, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has updated its growth scenario for the end of 2026. Accordingly, the average growth rate of the industrial production index in the remaining months of the year is expected to reach approximately 12.5 - 13%, ensuring that the whole year falls within the target range of 12 - 14%. Export turnover for the whole year is expected to increase by approximately 22.8%, total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue by approximately 13.3%, while the B2C (business-to-consumer) e-commerce market is expected to grow by approximately 20.5%.
Assessing growth prospects, in an interview with the Industry and Trade Newspaper, Dr. Le Duy Binh, Director of Economica Vietnam, stated that positive results in industrial production, trade, and consumption provide a basis for international organizations to adjust their assessments of Vietnam's economic outlook. Specifically, industrial production maintains high growth momentum, domestic purchasing power remains strong, and exports continue to be a prominent driving force.
The results achieved in the first nine months have laid an important foundation for the Ministry of Industry and Trade to continue pursuing its growth targets for 2026. However, achieving all eight targets comprehensively still requires focused efforts to overcome difficulties, especially for the two targets regarding total power generation capacity and B2C e-commerce growth in the remaining months of the year.
Identifying challenges in the final stretch

Despite positive performance results and growth forecasts, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has determined not to be complacent in the face of difficulties and challenges in the remaining months of the year. The results achieved ahead of schedule in the first nine months are considered a safe margin and will not be used to adjust down the operational requirements in the fourth quarter.
First, the international trade environment continues to be fraught with uncertainty. Export activities may face increasing pressure from trade protection measures, changes in tariff policies, and increasingly stringent environmental standards in major markets. Notably, the European Union has entered the formal implementation phase of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which requires businesses to control emissions, meet green standards, and enhance competitiveness.
Domestically, the storm and rainfall in the central region during October and November could affect production, transportation, and supply chains, requiring businesses to proactively develop response plans to minimize disruptions.
Notably, the pressure to achieve targets is concentrated on two priority indicators for the fourth quarter. For the electricity sector, the total power generation capacity currently stands at approximately 85,594.88 MW, requiring an additional 2,570 MW to reach a minimum of 88,165 MW by the end of the year. Meanwhile, the B2C e-commerce market grew by 19.5% after nine months, 0.5 percentage points lower than the lower end of the 20-22% target for the whole year. This necessitates accelerating growth in the remaining months of the year, while also improving the effectiveness of solutions to boost the market.
The above requirements indicate that, in order to build upon the achievements of the past nine months and comprehensively fulfill the 2026 targets, the Ministry of Industry and Trade needs to both maintain growth momentum in areas with positive results and focus on resolving difficulties related to indicators that are lagging behind schedule, ensuring that management is implemented proactively, flexibly, and effectively.
Managed on a monthly basis, with a firm commitment to achieving targets.
According to Official Letter No. 8293/BCT-KHTC dated October 12, 2026, the Ministry of Industry and Trade has established a unified operational scenario aimed at comprehensively achieving all targets for 2026, with a specific roadmap for October, November, and December. A notable point is the application of a three-tiered risk management mechanism (Green, Yellow, Red) for each target. When a target reaches the warning threshold, the lead unit must proactively activate the prepared solutions immediately, without waiting for the quarterly assessment results. In particular, a target must not remain at the Red level for more than one month without a solution and report.
For industrial production, the Ministry of Industry and Trade compiles a list of large enterprises, projects, and localities with large-scale industrial operations to monitor monthly output, prioritizing the assurance of electricity, gas, coal, and raw material supplies for production. At the same time, it urges the progress of bringing new industrial projects into operation in the fourth quarter, maximizing the capacity of oil refineries, fertilizer plants, steel mills, and cement factories to maintain industrial growth momentum in the remaining months of the year.
In the electricity sector, the Ministry of Industry and Trade requires the creation of a list of contingency projects with a total capacity of approximately 3,100 MW, equivalent to no less than 120% of the additional capacity needed. Simultaneously, it calls for accelerating the process of granting commercial operation permits for each unit and each part of the project that meets the requirements; shortening the time for conducting testing and acceptance procedures as stipulated, in order to bring power sources into operation as soon as possible. The Ministry is also proactively developing plans to respond to storms and floods, ensuring coal and gas reserves at power plants, and preparing electricity supply plans for the 2027 dry season.

For e-commerce, the Ministry of Industry and Trade is focusing on exploiting year-end shopping peaks and the 2026 Online Friday shopping event, coordinating with major e-commerce platforms to implement programs promoting the consumption of Vietnamese goods, supporting shipping and payment costs. According to the updated scenario, the growth rate of B2C e-commerce in October, November, and December is expected to reach 21%, 23%, and 26% respectively, aiming for a growth target of approximately 20.5% for the whole year.
Alongside promoting transactions, the Ministry of Industry and Trade is strengthening seller verification, ensuring transparency of product information, and managing cross-border e-commerce activities, aiming to build a healthy online business environment and protect consumer rights.
Regarding exports, the focus of management has shifted to maintaining a reasonable growth rate while improving the quality of growth. The Ministry of Industry and Trade is strengthening control over the origin of goods, enhancing the effectiveness of free trade agreements, expanding markets in the Middle East, Africa, and Latin America, and exploiting the potential of the Halal product market. Simultaneously, the Ministry is implementing the "GoGlobal" program for the period 2026-2030, as stipulated in Decision No. 626/QD-TTg of the Prime Minister , to support Vietnamese businesses in expanding their presence in international markets.

articles.title: Fashion Valet received close to RM40mil from Khazanah and PNB, court told - Free Malaysia Today
articles.summary: Fashion Valet received close to RM40mil from Khazanah and PNB, court told  Free Malaysia TodayFashionValet received investment of almost RM40mil from PNB and Khazanah, witness testifies  The StarFashion Valet received nearly RM40m from Khazanah, PNB in 2018, court told  MalaysiakiniCourt hears RM40m in Khazanah, PNB investments paid into Fashion Valet accounts  The VibesFashion Valet CBT trial: Khazanah, PNB pumped nearly RM40m into e-commerce firm, court ...
articles.full_text:
Public Bank manager Tay Lay Hong, 54, testified that Fashion Valet received RM7,848,000 and RM11,742,000 from Khazanah on March 23 and 26, respectively.
Tay said the company also received RM11,953,500 and RM8,364,966 from PNB on June 4 and Dec 20 in 2018, respectively.
Testifying in the RM8 million criminal breach of trust trial involving Fashion Valet founders Vivy Yusof and her husband, Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, she said RM11 million was disbursed from Fashion Valet’s account to undisclosed recipients on Aug 21 that year.
“I confirm that this was a fund disbursement transaction carried out through bulk payment via online banking,” she said in her witness statement.
Tay also said RM5 million was credited to Vivy’s Public Bank account on Sept 3 under the transaction reference “CIMB Rentas”, and another RM5 million was credited to Fadzarudin’s account the following day, marked as “interim dividend”.
Both transactions originated from 30 Maple Sdn Bhd, based on the bank records.
She said that on Sept 5, Vivy and Fadzarudin each withdrew RM5.5 million from their respective Public Bank accounts over the counter.
During cross-examination, defence counsel M Athimulan suggested that it was normal for a large retailer such as Fashion Valet to use bulk payments to meet financial commitments, including payroll, vendor bills and shop rentals.
Tay agreed.
Athimulan: That means the RM11 million transaction described as a bulk payment does not mean that it was transferred to any single personal account?
Tay: I agree.
Athimulan: You did not find any fraudulent transfers in this bulk payment to shell companies or non-existent personal accounts?
Tay: I agree.
Vivy and Fadzarudin, both 38, were jointly charged on Dec 5, 2024 with committing criminal breach of trust involving investment funds from Khazanah and PNB in their capacity as directors of Fashion Valet.
They are accused of authorising a payment of RM8 million from Fashion Valet’s corporate bank account to 30 Maple Sdn Bhd without board approval on Aug 21, 2018, at Public Bank’s Bukit Damansara branch.
The charge was framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Vivy and Fadzarudin also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge of dishonestly misappropriating RM8 million in Khazanah and PNB investment funds belonging to Fashion Valet at the same location on the same date.
The charge under Section 403 of the Penal Code carries a jail term of between six months and five years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The trial before judge Rosli Ahmad continues on Nov 3.

articles.title: Expectations to reduce the trade deficit. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Expectations to reduce the trade deficit.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Increased imports are linked to cycles of production expansion.
 The outlook for goods exports at the end of the year remains positive, with nearly 31% of businesses forecasting an increase in new export orders in Q4 2026, while 54.2% expect stability and only 15% forecast a decrease compared to Q3.
 Along with total import and export turnover reaching 888 billion USD in the first nine months, a 30.4% increase compared to the same period last year, the order survey results show that trade activity is maintaining its growth momentum. This provides a basis for expecting that exports for the whole year may exceed the growth target of 15-16%, while also contributing to improving the trade balance.
 However, the task now is not only to maintain the export growth momentum but also to find solutions to narrow the trade deficit of $19.4 billion after nine months. 
 Focus on exploiting export markets. In the fourth quarter, export activities should focus on further exploring markets with remaining growth potential, especially the US and EU; leveraging the advantages of free trade agreements, while also boosting exports of high-demand product groups such as electronics, machinery, agricultural products, and seafood.  Although the trade balance remains in deficit, the structure of imported goods shows that the majority of the value directly serves production.
 According to statistics, the group of production materials reached US$426.92 billion, accounting for 94.1% of total import turnover. Of which, machinery, equipment, tools, and spare parts accounted for 58.3%; raw materials, fuels, and supplies accounted for 35.8%. The group of consumer goods accounted for only 5.9%.
 Therefore, the sharp increase in import turnover in the first nine months of 2026 should not be viewed solely as a negative sign. The majority of imported goods are machinery, equipment, raw materials, and fuels, meeting the needs for expanding production, investment, and exports in the coming period.
 "Therefore, for both export and import goods, we are currently importing mainly raw materials to serve production, not an increase in the import of non-essential consumer goods," affirmed Ms. Trinh Thi Thu Hien, Deputy Director of the Import-Export Department (Ministry of Industry and Trade).
 Besides increased input demand, price fluctuations and component supply also contribute to imports growing faster than exports, especially in the electronics industry. When raw material prices rise sharply, the value of imports in foreign currency also increases, even if the quantity of goods imported remains unchanged.
 Contract prices for some high-end memory chips used in mobile phones and tablets have increased by approximately 300-500% year-on-year, amid a global shortage of mobile device memory chips due to a wave of investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.
 "If a company imported 1,000 chips last year and imports the same quantity this year, but the price of chips has increased sharply, then the import value will increase accordingly. In fact, some businesses within the Samsung system have shown that, although they still have a trade surplus, the surplus has decreased compared to the same period last year due to the high increase in input material prices," a representative from the Ministry of Industry and Trade stated.
 Another reason is that businesses are increasing their raw material reserves to ensure production operations amidst unstable supply. Through working with several electronics and computer manufacturing companies, the Import-Export Department noted that many factories and businesses in multinational supply chains have proactively increased their inventory levels to prevent potential supply disruptions.
 "Some businesses now have inventory reserves that last until March 2027. For example, the inventory reserve cycle, which used to be typically 6 weeks, has now been extended to 12 weeks in some cases," Ms. Hien informed.
 In some businesses, the value of raw material inventory has increased from approximately $100 million to $700 million. When the figures from these businesses are combined, this increase in reserves also contributed to a sharp increase in the overall import value of the electronics industry.
 In the first nine months of 2026, imports of computers, electronic products, and components reached $188.9 billion, a 71.7% increase compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, exports of this product group reached $123.6 billion, resulting in a trade deficit exceeding $65 billion for this group alone.
 Regarding the rate of import growth, Mr. Phan Duc Hieu, a National Assembly representative and member of the National Assembly's Economic and Financial Committee, believes that import and export trends need to be considered within the overall growth model of the economy, linked to the process of integration, attracting investment, expanding markets, and the requirement to increase domestic value.
 The current import structure shows that the majority of goods are used for production, export, and investment. Notably, by September 30, 2026, the total registered FDI capital in Vietnam reached US$50.36 billion, an increase of 76.4% compared to the same period last year. Actual FDI reached over US$21 billion, an increase of 12.1% and the highest level in the past five years.
 According to Mr. Hieu, in the context of a volatile world , trade activities are increasingly difficult to predict and are heavily impacted by costs and prices. Therefore, it is necessary to carefully analyze the quality and structure of imports, instead of just looking at the increase in value to assess the trade balance.
 Opportunities to improve the trade balance.
 Further discussing this year's trade balance, Ms. Trinh Thi Thu Hien stated that Government Resolution No. 01/NQ-CP sets a target of approximately 15-16% growth in export turnover.
 "With total import and export turnover reaching 888 billion USD, the trade balance for the first nine months showed a deficit of 19.4 billion USD, a surplus of 1.27 billion USD in September, and the end of the year is the peak season for exports. Therefore, we have grounds to expect that the trade deficit in the remaining months of the year and for the whole of 2026 could fall below 10 billion USD," Ms. Hien expected.
 Traditionally, the fourth quarter is a period when trade activity tends to remain high. The scale of exports and imports in the third quarter increased sharply, reaching nearly $118 billion in September alone. However, the outlook for the trade balance in the remaining months of the year will depend on the interplay between the rate of export growth and the demand for imported inputs.
 On the positive side, exports are showing signs of accelerating. In the third quarter, export turnover increased by 30.4% compared to the same period last year, higher than the 24.5% increase in the first nine months. In September alone, exports increased by 39.1%, indicating a significant improvement in growth rate in recent months.
 Conversely, imports continue to grow faster than exports. In the third quarter, import value increased by 42.2%; in September alone, it increased by 45.8% compared to the same period last year. If the demand for raw materials, components, and machinery continues to increase along with production, the pressure from imports will be difficult to alleviate quickly.
 In this context, the potential for improving the trade balance in the fourth quarter depends on whether exports continue to accelerate and imports slow down. If the growth gap between exports and imports narrows, the trade balance could turn more positive.
 However, with a trade deficit of $19.4 billion after nine months, to bring the full-year deficit below $10 billion, Vietnam needs to achieve a trade surplus of over $9.4 billion in the fourth quarter. This is not an easy condition to meet, given the high demand for imported raw materials and components for production.
 Nevertheless, the improved outlook for export orders at the end of the year, coupled with the fact that many businesses have proactively stockpiled raw materials, could create more favorable conditions for production and export activities. The extent of improvement in the trade balance will depend on the ability to take advantage of these conditions, as well as price developments and market demand.
 Vietnam's trade volume has been continuously expanding over the years. It is projected to reach US$930 billion in 2025, while it is expected to surpass US$1.2 trillion in 2026 if the current growth momentum is maintained. Alongside this, the structure of export goods is shifting towards an increased proportion of processed and manufactured industrial products, contributing to Vietnam's increasingly deeper participation in global production networks and supply chains.
 To ensure that the quality of growth is commensurate with the ever-increasing scale of trade, Mr. Phan Duc Hieu proposed focusing on developing value chains led by Vietnamese businesses, through investment in forming domestic enterprises capable of playing a leading role. At the same time, he suggested gradually increasing the localization rate and reducing dependence on imports for raw materials and components that Vietnam is capable of producing.
 In addition, it is necessary to strictly enforce the requirement for transparency of origin for products exported to markets where Vietnam has a large trade surplus, thereby reducing trade risks, protecting the reputation of Vietnamese goods, and creating a foundation for more sustainable export growth.

articles.title: Choose the right breakthrough area to achieve growth targets of 10% or more. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Choose the right breakthrough area to achieve growth targets of 10% or more.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Chairman of the National Assembly's Economic and Finance Committee, Phan Van Mai, emphasized that to achieve a growth target of 10% or more in 2027, the crucial factor is selecting the right breakthrough areas, improving implementation efficiency, productivity, and the self-reliance of the economy.
On the morning of October 17th, at the opening session of the 2nd meeting of the 16th National Assembly, Phan Van Mai, Chairman of the National Assembly's Economic and Finance Committee , presented a report on the review of the implementation of the socio-economic development plan for 2026 and the projected plan for 2027.
High growth but an unstable foundation.
The National Assembly 's agencies highly appreciate the decisive and flexible leadership and management of the Government and the Prime Minister, as well as the efforts of ministries, sectors, and localities, contributing to achieving important results in the implementation of the socio-economic development plan for 2026.
However, the Economic and Financial Committee noted that while growth is high, the foundation is not yet solid. The four localities with the largest economies, including Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi , Hai Phong, and Dong Nai, which account for nearly 47% of the country's total GRDP, are all projected to fall short of their growth targets for 2026.
Furthermore, private investment has not truly broken through, accounting for 53% of total social investment but only increasing by 14%, the lowest among the three sectors. According to statistics, exports increased by 24.5% but imports increased by 36.7%, resulting in a trade deficit of $19.42 billion. At the same time, exports are still heavily dependent on the FDI sector, while supporting industries, localization rates, and technological mastery capabilities remain limited.
"Growth in scale has not gone hand in hand with increased productivity, domestically generated added value, and the self-reliance of the economy," Comrade Phan Van Mai stated.
Pressure to maintain macroeconomic stability and financial security is increasing. The average CPI for the first nine months rose by 4.52%, already at the target of around 4.5% for the whole year; the increase in the third quarter alone was 4.8%. Prices of essential goods and services are rising, while real purchasing power is recovering slowly.
Credit growth has outpaced deposit mobilization, resulting in a high credit-to-GDP ratio. The capital market has not adequately met medium- and long-term needs, placing a heavy burden of capital supply on the banking system and increasing the risk of maturity mismatches and liquidity pressure.
Risks in banking, corporate bonds, and real estate are interconnected and easily amplify each other, while room for further monetary policy easing is increasingly limited.

Large resources, but limited implementation effectiveness.
According to the audit report, significant investment resources have been slow to be transformed into new production capacity and growth drivers. Public investment disbursement in the first nine months reached 62.9% of the plan, but unrecovered advance payments accounted for 37% of the disbursed amount. Several key projects are behind schedule; and 1,131 outstanding projects have solutions in place but have not yet been resolved.
Power generation and transmission grid projects, especially LNG power projects, are progressing slowly; energy storage capacity is limited, posing potential risks to energy security.
Regarding science and technology, despite allocating approximately 95,000 billion VND, only 37.26% has been disbursed after 9 months, leaving about 24,000 billion VND unallocated. Investment in strategic technologies is not commensurate with the investment.
"The core issue lies not only in the scale of resources but also in the quality of preparation, allocation, absorption capacity, and implementation effectiveness," the report states, while also pointing out that organizational implementation remains a bottleneck despite accelerated institutional reforms.
The business and household sector also faces many difficulties. In the first nine months, the number of businesses entering and re-entering the market decreased by 3.2%, while the number of businesses completing dissolution procedures increased by 118.8%. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have difficulty accessing capital and are under pressure from input costs, logistics, and compliance costs.
Household businesses are facing a slow recovery in purchasing power while simultaneously adapting to the demands of digital transformation , governance, and tax policies.
Comrade Phan Van Mai stated that these difficulties directly affect investment, employment, income, and domestic demand; youth unemployment remains high.
Clearly define responsibilities, deadlines, and expected outcomes.
Regarding 2027, the Chairman of the Economic and Financial Committee noted that the global context is projected to remain complex and unpredictable. The operational scenario needs to take into account the delayed effects of the 2026 shocks, especially the possibility of continued high energy prices and "suppressed" inflation as tax and fee support measures are adjusted.

According to the review agency, the target of GDP growth of 10% or more demonstrates strong determination but poses significant challenges given the unstable growth foundation, inflationary pressures, and increasing demand for capital and energy.
The government's system of tasks and solutions for 2027 needs to overcome the problem of being too scattered and clarify priorities. With a growth target of 10% or more, the decisive issue is not adding more solutions, but rather choosing the right breakthroughs, improving implementation efficiency, productivity, and the self-reliance of the economy.
The Economic and Financial Committee's review report clearly states this.
The Economic and Financial Committee proposed that the Government focus on implementing six key areas, emphasizing that implementation is the decisive factor. Accordingly, it is necessary to clearly define the responsibilities, deadlines, resources, and outputs of each task; strengthen inspection and supervision, and link implementation results to the responsibility of the head of each agency.

articles.title: Open up room for growth, but do not abandon risk management. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Open up room for growth, but do not abandon risk management.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Separating certain loans for restaurants, hotels, tourism, resorts, and key projects from the credit growth limit (room) is creating more room for banks to expand lending. However, experts believe that this "separation" is only meaningful when accompanied by a strict appraisal, disbursement, and monitoring mechanism, avoiding turning credit room into easily available capital.
According to Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam Pham Thanh Ha, as of September 30th, outstanding credit in the entire system reached VND 20.75 million billion, an increase of 11.59% compared to the end of 2025 and 16.69% compared to the same period last year. In the context of high economic growth targets, the challenge is to simultaneously expand credit to the economy while maintaining system stability and controlling inflation.

One of the solutions implemented by the State Bank of Vietnam is to create room for credit institutions to provide funding to certain sectors that are crucial to growth. Accordingly, outstanding loans for social housing, industrial parks, export processing zones; restaurants, hotels, tourist areas, eco-tourism and resort areas are not included in the controlled real estate credit outstanding. Similarly, credit granted to businesses for the implementation and investment of large-scale, key projects with a ripple effect and linkages that promote regional and local economic development to achieve double-digit growth targets are not included in the overall controlled credit outstanding.
It's important to note that this mechanism doesn't mean banks can disregard credit limits or loan quality. Essentially, it's a way to classify and manage loans with specific characteristics, serving production and business activities and generating cash flow, so that they don't completely overlap with other investment and business-oriented real estate loans.
Economist Dr. Nguyen Minh Phong believes that separating tourism credit from real estate credit is reasonable, as this sector has room for growth and many projects have the potential to generate cash flow. By no longer being directly included in the controlled real estate loan portfolio, banks will have more room to disburse funds to businesses investing in accommodation, services, and tourism infrastructure.
You may also like
For key projects, the benefits are even clearer. According to Mr. Phong, many large projects only have about 15% of their capital from the investor, with the rest significantly dependent on bank credit. If all these loans were included in the real estate lending limit, banks could quickly reach their limit, thereby narrowing their ability to provide funding for other sectors. Separating policy-related loans and creating a ripple effect therefore helps avoid a situation where a single large project "occupies" too much of the credit limit.
Separate the rooms, but don't separate the risks.
According to Mr. Le Quoc Minh, Deputy General Director of Military Commercial Bank (MB), excluding loans for restaurants, hotels, and resorts from the real estate sector will create more room for banks and businesses, especially for service industries that play a crucial role in economic development. However, not including these loans in a specific credit limit does not change the bank's responsibility for the quality of the loan.
Mr. Minh argued that when appraising a project, banks still need to fully assess its legal status, the developer's capacity, and its ability to repay the loan. This is an indispensable "barrier," regardless of whether the loan is eligible for a special lending mechanism or not.
Dr. Nguyen Minh Phong also noted that the biggest risk lies not in the separation of loan portfolios, but in how banks disburse and monitor loans after disbursement. According to him, capital should be disbursed according to the project's progress and actual needs, instead of being disbursed all at once or too easily, thereby limiting the risk of misuse of funds.
At the same time, loans in specific categories need to be subject to transparent information, reporting, and regular inspections. For large-scale projects, banks need to develop their own governance criteria and contingency plans for when project progress, cash flow, or the investor's financial capacity deteriorates.
This requirement is all the more noteworthy given the rapid increase in real estate credit. According to the Ministry of Construction , by the end of June 2026, outstanding credit for real estate business activities reached over 2,519 trillion VND, an increase of 12.71% compared to the end of the first quarter, equivalent to an increase of over 284,000 billion VND in just one quarter. Notably, credit for industrial park and export processing zone construction projects increased by 32.38%, while outstanding credit for eco-tourism and resort projects decreased by 4.35%, and credit for restaurant and hotel projects decreased by 0.16%.

These figures show that "decentralizing the lending" is essentially a reclassification of capital flows, rather than a shift from controlled to free-flowing. Priority loans may have better access to capital, but will still be subject to full requirements regarding credit assessment, credit quality, capital adequacy, and risk management.
In the final months of the year, the State Bank of Vietnam announced that it will continue to refine credit mechanisms and policies; direct capital into priority sectors and growth drivers, while strictly controlling credit in sectors with potential risks.
The challenge, therefore, is not about "opening or closing the credit limit," but about opening it in the right places and controlling the risks correctly. When credit is separated from the general limit but still within a rigorous appraisal, disbursement, and monitoring process, the credit limit truly becomes a tool for allocating capital for growth instead of a new source of risk for the system.
